text_simplified: The text speaks of the importance of tarbiyah of children upon noble akhlaq and patience when angered. It mentions a story of a man who became angry, so the Prophet ﷺ advised him to seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan. It also points to the rights of children over their parents in guidance and tarbiyah.

review_defects.why: The English phrase is not idiomatic; 'Patience at Anger' could be misread as patience directed at anger rather than patience during anger. Better: 'Patience When Angry' or 'Patience at the Time of Anger'.

review_defects.english: rights of children over their parents
review_defects.why: The Arabic preposition 'على' indicates an obligation upon parents, not authority of children over parents. 'Over' may imply control; 'upon' is more accurate.
